headline: Public Law 115-56 keeps federal agencies funded through December 8, 2017, adds $15.25 billion in disaster relief, and temporarily suspends the federal debt limit.
what_it_does: The law is a continuing resolution that funds most federal agencies at fiscal year 2017 levels, reduced by 0.6791%, so a government shutdown does not start on October 1, 2017. It provides $15.25 billion in emergency aid for hurricane recovery through FEMA, the Small Business Administration, and HUD. It also suspends the public debt limit until December 9, 2017, and includes a separate section on U.S. support for basic education in developing countries.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies can keep paying staff and running programs at a set funding rate, which helps them avoid furloughs, though new programs generally cannot start.

who_it_affects.group: People affected by Hurricanes Harvey and Irma
who_it_affects.how: The $15.25 billion in emergency funds is directed to FEMA disaster relief, SBA disaster loans, and HUD community development block grants.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses and homeowners hit by disasters
who_it_affects.how: The bill provides $450 million for SBA disaster loan programs.

who_it_affects.group: Low-income elderly people receiving food assistance
who_it_affects.how: The Commodity Supplemental Food Program is allowed to operate at a higher rate than otherwise permitted under the continuing resolution.
The law sets specific rules for how base grant amounts are calculated while the continuing resolution is in effect.
The law changes a funding limit for the Child Enrollment Contingency Fund and makes a rescission from the program.

who_it_affects.group: People who visit federal recreational lands
who_it_affects.how: Federal agencies may keep collecting and using recreation fees through September 30, 2019.

who_it_affects.group: Homeowners with flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program
who_it_affects.how: The program's authorization is extended under the continuing resolution.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans receiving care at VA facilities
who_it_affects.how: Funds for repairs from Hurricane Sandy damage at a VA construction account remain available for longer.

who_it_affects.group: Children and communities in developing countries receiving U.S. education aid
who_it_affects.how: The law sets a U.S. policy to promote basic education abroad and requires the President to produce a five-year strategy and an annual report to Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: Most provisions took effect when the law was signed on September 8, 2017; the funding and debt limit suspension run through December 8, 2017, and the foreign education strategy is due within one year.
